s1.where: the empty page with the greeting and the writing box at the bottom
s1.expectation: Probably the start screen where I would type a new message to Claude.
s1.cue: Nothing names it. The 'Chat with Claude...' box at the bottom and the empty middle suggest a new conversation. The large text is a greeting, 'Back at it, Ally Cooper'.

first_pass.why: 'Back at it, Ally Cooper' is a greeting to a person, not the name of a place. Nothing on the screen names this screen. I only infer it is the start page from the empty writing box at the bottom.
first_pass.solution: Put a literal title at the top, the same place other screens put theirs, such as 'New chat'. Keep the greeting if you want, but not as the only text.

test_cases.task: The app opens on the page with the large greeting in the middle and the writing box at the bottom (if it is not already there: open the menu with the three lines at the top left and tap the big word at the top of the menu). Put the phone down, look away and count slowly to ten, then look back at the screen and, before touching anything, say where you are. Then drag the page up and down and watch whether a name for this page shows up anywhere. (The picture with the microphone warning cannot be brought back without the phone's permission prompts, so answer for that picture from this same page.)
test_cases.real_if: you still have to work out where you are from the writing box, and no name for the page appears anywhere
test_cases.not_real_if: you know straight away where you are, or a name for the page shows up
test_cases.persona_report: When I looked back I still had to work it out from the 'Chat with Claude...' box. The big text now says 'Good afternoon, Ally Cooper' where the picture said 'Back at it, Ally Cooper', so the only large text on the page changes by itself between visits. Dragging up and down moved nothing, and no name for the page appeared anywhere. The top bar only has the three-line menu icon and the ghost icon. Later, when I came back to this page from the menu, the keyboard opened again without me asking.
test_cases.what_they_did: The app was already on the greeting page, but the keyboard had opened by itself. I closed it with Back once. I looked away and back, then said where I was before touching anything. Then I dragged the page up and down.

s1.closing_comment: No name appears anywhere, and the one big piece of text is a greeting that changes between visits ('Back at it' then 'Good afternoon'), so it cannot even serve as a landmark.

test_cases.task: From the page with the greeting, tap the small microphone picture in the writing box (the grey one, not the round black button at the far right). On the page that opens, tap the box headed 'Speech Input Language' so its list drops down. Without choosing anything, say where you are. Then press the phone's Back button once to close the list, and compare. Do not press Continue. Leave with the X at the top left.
test_cases.real_if: while the list is open nothing tells you what page this is
test_cases.not_real_if: you can still tell what page this is while the list is open
test_cases.persona_report: With the list open, the screen matched the picture exactly: a drawing of a microphone, a list of languages with a tick on English, and 'Speech Input Language' underneath. No title. The list covers the sentence 'Send messages to Claude using your voice.' On the phone I knew where I was only because I had just tapped the box myself two seconds earlier. The screen itself did not tell me. Back closed the list and the sentence came back. It was already on this page and did not move, so it is a fixed place I can check once the list is shut.
test_cases.what_they_did: From the greeting page I tapped the grey microphone in the writing box. The voice setup page slid up. I tapped the 'Speech Input Language' box and the language list dropped down. Without choosing anything, I said where I was. I pressed Back once to close the list and compared. Then I left with the X, without pressing Continue.

s14.closing_comment: In the frozen picture nothing names the page, and that is still true. On the phone I had just opened the list myself, and one Back press brought the sentence back, so in practice I was not lost for long.

test_cases.task: Open the menu (three lines, top left) and tap Artifacts. Tap the small picture at the top right and choose Pinned; say which list you are now looking at. test_cases.persona_report: After choosing Pinned, the top-right button turned into a blue circle with a pin drawn in it. The word beside the search box still said 'All', and the middle said 'No artifacts match'. What is written says All, and it was not All. After choosing Code, the word said 'Code' but the pin filter was still only the blue picture. The only written place that showed 'Pinned' was the menu itself, with a tick, and only while it was open. So two filters were on, and only one was ever written on the page.
test_cases.what_they_did: I opened the menu and tapped Artifacts. I tapped the small picture at the top right and chose Pinned, then said which list I was on. Next I tapped the word beside the search box ('All') and chose Code, then said which list I was on. Then I put both back: small picture, choose All; word beside the search box, choose All. Both show All again.

s46.closing_comment: On the real app the written word said 'All' while the Pinned filter was on. The page tells me the wrong thing in words, not just nothing.
